description.value: The study examined how threat predictability and controllability affect threat-elicited neural responses during yoked Pavlovian fear conditioning in healthy humans.

spans.text: The present study investigated the effect of predictability and controllability on the threat-elicited neurophysiological response to better understand the underlying processes that support emotional resilience.

stimuli.value: Two tones and a loud white-noise UCS.

spans.text: Two tones (700 and 1300 Hz; 10 s duration; 20 s ITI) served as the CSs and a loud (100 dB) white-noise served as the UCS
They were instructed that they could terminate the UCS by making a single button press on the joystick.

instructions.value: Controllable-condition participants were told that the UCS would last 0.5–6.0 seconds and that they could terminate it with a single joystick button press; if they did not press, it would last 6.0 seconds. Uncontrollable-condition participants were told the same duration range but could not terminate the UCS and were instructed to press a button when it ended to control for motor activity. Participants continuously rated UCS expectancy from 0 to 100.
